official.deadline_note: All application materials are due October 1, 2027; the three letters of recommendation are due one week later on October 8, 2027, and an application is not eligible for review until all three letters are received. No separate institutional deadline is published.
official.status_note: The Center states it will begin accepting applications for the 2028-29 academic year on July 1, 2027, with a deadline of October 1, 2027; the 2027-28 competition is no longer accepting applications as of verification.
benefits: Individually determined stipend: 'The stipend amounts awarded are individually determined, according to the needs of the Fellow and the Center's ability to meet them. The Center seeks to provide half salary with the expectation that the Fellow's home institution covers the remaining salary.'

Round trip travel to the NHC at the beginning of the fellowship term and the return trip home at the end of the term, for the Fellow and any immediate family members traveling and living with the Fellow in North Carolina during the fellowship year

A private study overlooking the woods, exceptional library services (procurement of books, articles, AV materials and archival scans, in-depth reference assistance, training in electronic research tools), and weekday breakfasts and lunches in the Teachers' Commons
J-1 (Research Scholar) visa sponsorship for Fellows who are not U.S. citizens, with J-2 sponsorship for legal spouses and unmarried children under 21
eligibility: Holds a PhD or relevant terminal degree for their primary discipline (e.g., MFA for research-based non-fiction writers)

The PhD or requisite terminal degree was received at least five years prior to October 1, 2027 (i.e., no later than September 30, 2022), unless applying for the Geiss-Hsu Fellowship or the Philip L. Quinn Fellowship
Has published at least one scholarly monograph, for book-focused fields, or the equivalent in peer-reviewed scholarship for article-focused fields
Is working on a project beyond the dissertation and engaged in humanities research that will result in publication
The proposed project is at an advanced stage: most of the research is done and the applicant is already writing
Plans to spend the full term (one or two semesters) in residence at the Center; extended time away, including trips for field research, is not permitted
requirements: All materials due October 1, 2027; letters of recommendation due October 8, 2027
Project proposal, 1,000 words maximum, in 11- or 12-point font with margins no smaller than one inch; must note the current stage of the project and the projected timeline to completion
Curriculum vitae, four pages maximum, including previous book-length publications
One-page tentative outline noting the stage or projected completion date for each chapter, section or module
Three letters of recommendation; the portal requires three unique referee email addresses
documents: One-page tentative outline of the structure of the project
Three letters of recommendation submitted by referees through the portal
selection_criteria: Fellows are chosen based not on their record of past achievements but on the strength of their project proposal and its supporting documents
The proposal must be clear to an interdisciplinary audience unfamiliar with the topic or the terminology of the field; overly specialized language is discouraged
Recommendations that speak specifically to the merits of the project are more effective than letters from famous scholars who do not know the applicant's work
Proposals and outlines that do not explicitly address project status and projected timeline or completion stages are deemed ineligible
coverage: Individually determined stipend (the Center seeks to provide about half of the Fellow's salary)
Round trip travel for the Fellow and any immediate family members traveling and living with the Fellow in North Carolina during the fellowship year
The stipend is salary replacement only: no indirect costs or fringe benefits are built into the stipend amounts and institutional overhead is not allowed
No additional funding is provided for research travel, edited letters or primary source document collections, moving expenses, shipping expenses, or living expenses
application_method: Complete the online application through the Center's application portal
Upload the proposal, bibliography, CV and one-page outline
Provide the names and contact information of three references, who receive an email prompt inviting them to upload a letter of recommendation
official.application_route: Apply online through the Center's application portal: submit the application and upload the four documents by October 1, then have all three referees upload letters by October 8.
official.study_mode: Full-time residential; the full term (one or two semesters) must be spent in residence at the Center and partial terms cannot be accommodated
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship requirements; international applicants are warmly invited to apply
official.international_eligibility: Yes - applicants of any citizenship or national origin are eligible. The Center sponsors J-1 Research Scholar visas for Fellows who are not U.S. citizens (J-2 for legal spouses and unmarried children under 21); exchange visitors must satisfy English language proficiency and medical insurance requirements
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The project must be grounded in one or more humanities disciplines, or grounded in other fields (natural and social sciences, the arts, the professions, public life) but substantially employing humanistic approaches and methodologies; creative writing, dissertation-derived projects, and explicitly pedagogical works are excluded
official.research_requirement: A substantial humanistic scholarly project at an advanced stage - most research complete, writing already begun - described in a 1,000-word proposal that states how far the work has progressed and what the applicant hopes to accomplish at the Center
official.duration: Academic year (September through May), fall semester (September through December), or spring semester (January through May)
official.description: The National Humanities Center is a private, nonprofit organization and the only independent institute dedicated exclusively to advanced study in all areas of the humanities. It describes its Residential Fellowship as one of the most prestigious humanities fellowship programs in the world, offering scholars the time, space and support to pursue their work and take part in a vibrant intellectual community.
official.program_type: Independent humanities institute research fellowship (private nonprofit)
official.english_requirement: Fluency in written and spoken English is required (the applicant speaks and reads English fluently); no IELTS/TOEFL score is published. J-1 exchange visitors must additionally satisfy English language proficiency and medical insurance requirements.

verification.notes: Both official pages (Residential Fellowships and the FAQ) were read in full; stipend wording, travel reimbursement, document rules and the 2028-29 timeline come from them. The Center publishes no fixed stipend figure - stipends are individually determined as partial salary replacement - so funding amount, currency and period are recorded as null rather than estimated.

applicant_utility.summary: This is salary replacement, not a graduate scholarship: the NHC sets each stipend individually and states only that it seeks to provide about half of your salary, expecting your home institution to cover the rest. You must live at the Center in Durham, North Carolina for the full term (September-May or one semester), so budget for housing, local transport and moving costs the Center never pays. The competition opens once a year on July 1 and closes October 1, with reference letters landing a week later, so the writing has to be substantially done before you apply.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior humanities scholars with a published monograph or substantial peer-reviewed record - including independent, non-tenure-track, HBCU and international scholars - who need a protected residential writing term and can secure institutional leave.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your degree date: the PhD or terminal degree must have been earned no later than September 30, 2022 for the 2028-29 round; only the Geiss-Hsu (Ming-era China) and Philip L. Quinn (early-career female philosopher) fellowships waive this
Confirm you meet the publication bar (at least one single-authored monograph or the equivalent in peer-reviewed scholarship) before drafting a proposal
End the 1,000-word proposal with an explicit account of how far the research has gone and what remains - omitting status and timeline makes the project ineligible, not merely weak
Trim the CV to four pages and the bibliography to two, keeping the outline to one page with a completion stage for every chapter or section
Line up three referees early, each with a unique email address, and tell them the letters are due a week after your own deadline
If institution-based, inform your institution before applying, and remember the salary you enter at application is the salary your stipend offer will be calculated from
common_rejection_risks: Proposals or outlines that fail to state project status, projected timeline or completion stages are deemed ineligible outright
Applications missing any of the three recommendation letters are not eligible for review, and referees control that final week
Dissertation-derived projects, edited volumes, primary-source collections, creative writing, syllabi and textbooks, and non-humanities deliverables such as white papers are excluded
Long absences: this is a residential writing fellowship, and absences of 10 consecutive days or more may not be approved
Applying while still finishing the PhD or within five years of the degree without qualifying for one of the two designated fellowships
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing and daily living expenses in Durham for the whole term (the Center funds no living expenses), local transportation - effectively a car, since public transit is inadequate - research travel, moving and shipping, plus usually the remaining share of salary; the stipend is taxable and carries no fringe benefits or overhead.
document_audit: Upload PDFs: the portal converts Word files and can distort formatting and drop non-English characters, which can push a document over its word or page limit
Word and page limits are enforced on the converted PDF, so stay comfortably inside them rather than exactly at the boundary
The portal needs three distinct referee email addresses; if one person uploads all letters, referees can forward their portal logins to that person
Dossier services such as Interfolio are accepted, but you must enter the dossier-assigned email in place of the referee's own address
Reviewers may rank a longer, less focused CV lower, so keep it to four pages maximum and list prior book-length publications
Nothing can be changed after submission, so proofread the converted PDFs before you confirm
alerts: The 2028-29 window opens July 1, 2027 and closes October 1, 2027; the 2027-28 round has already closed, so plan your writing calendar for next July
Materials due October 1 but letters due October 8 - your file is incomplete until every letter is in the portal
No edits of any kind are possible once the application is submitted, by you or by the Center
A raise received after you apply will not raise your stipend; the offer is based on the salary listed at application
Former Fellows may reapply only once the previous fellowship project has been published and at least five years have passed since the last successful application
Applicants are emailed their status in February, the class is announced in early April, and alternates are called by the vice president for scholarly programs
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the application in the Center's online portal, upload the four PDFs by October 1, send the reference requests early, then watch for the confirmation email and track all three letters in the portal until each shows as uploaded.
